GFC Hair Treatment

Hair fall that won't stop, a widening part or a thinning crown? GFC (Growth Factor Concentrate) takes the growth factors from a small sample of your own blood and puts them right where your hair is thinning. It's more concentrated than PRP, needs no surgery, and you can go back to work the same day.

45–60 minPer session

Treatment overview

What is GFC (Growth Factor Concentrate)?

Your blood carries platelets, and platelets are full of growth factors: natural proteins your body uses to repair and build tissue. Hair follicles respond to these same signals.

In GFC treatment, we draw a small amount of your blood and process it in special GFC tubes. The tubes make the platelets release their growth factors, which are then separated into a clear, concentrated liquid. This is injected into the thinning areas of your scalp to wake up weak follicles, slow hair fall and grow thicker hair.

Read more: why thin hair needs growth factors

Every hair grows, rests and sheds in a cycle. Healthy hair spends years in the growing phase. When hormones, stress, illness, poor nutrition or genetics get in the way, follicles shrink, their growing phase gets shorter and each new hair comes in thinner.

Growth factors help reverse that. They improve blood supply to the root, help follicle cells multiply and keep hair in the growing phase for longer. Read more about the causes of hair loss.

1. ConcentrateGrowth factors are released from your platelets and collected.
2. InjectFine injections place them at the roots of thinning hair.
3. RegrowFollicles strengthen and grow thicker hair over the next few months.

From your blood to your scalp

How GFC Is Made, Step by Step

The whole process happens in the clinic, in one visit, in about an hour.

1. A small blood draw

About 20 to 30 ml of blood is taken from your arm, just like a routine blood test.

2. Special GFC tubes

The blood goes into sterile GFC tubes that make your platelets release their growth factors.

3. Spin and separate

A centrifuge separates the growth-factor-rich liquid from the red cells and platelets.

4. Inject where it's thin

The concentrate is injected with a very fine needle across the thinning areas of your scalp.

Find your plan

Answer two quick questions to see the plan our doctors most often recommend. We confirm your final plan after examining your scalp.

Fuller Part Plan

In women, thinning usually shows as a wider part and flatter crown. GFC thickens existing strands and helps new growth along the part.

The crown thins quietly, and most people only notice it in photos. GFC targets the thin patch to improve density and coverage.

What to expect

Benefits of GFC Hair Treatment

Your own growth factors, in a stronger and cleaner form.

Less Hair Fall

Strengthens weak roots so you see fewer hairs on your pillow, comb and bathroom floor.

Regrowth in Thin Areas

Wakes up resting follicles along the hairline, parting and crown.

Thicker Strands

Thin, wispy hairs grow back with more body, so hair looks fuller.

From Your Own Blood

Made from a small sample of your blood, so there's no risk of allergy to a foreign product.

Concentrated & Cell-Free

Growth factors are released and collected before injection, without the platelets and cells that PRP carries.

Less Soreness Than PRP

With no cells to trigger swelling, most people find GFC more comfortable afterwards.

Fewer Sessions

Because it's more concentrated, many people need fewer sessions than with PRP.

No Surgery, No Downtime

Walk out and get back to work the same day.

Swipe to see more

Is it right for you?

Hair Problems GFC Can Help With

Tap a concern to see how GFC helps, what we pair it with and how many sessions you may need.

Excessive hair fall

Losing up to 100 hairs a day is normal. Clumps in the shower, a thinner ponytail or hair all over your pillow means too many follicles have slipped into the resting phase. GFC sends strong growth signals that push them back into growing.

  • Shedding slows, often after 1 to 2 sessions
  • Stronger, better-anchored roots
  • Works best once the cause is found
Often combined withBlood testsNutrition
Typical sessions3–4, every 4 weeks
Hair loss causes and treatments

Male pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia)

A receding hairline, thinning temples or a thin crown in men is caused by DHT, a hormone that slowly shrinks follicles. GFC strengthens shrinking follicles and thickens the hair that's left. Prescribed medication protects them from DHT.

  • Holds and thickens the hairline
  • Thicker hair at the temples and crown
  • Best results when started early
Often combined withPrescribed medicationExosomes
Typical sessions4–6, then maintenance
Men's hair loss solutions

Female pattern hair loss

Women rarely go bald. Instead, the part widens and the top looks flat. It's often linked to hormones, PCOS, thyroid problems or low iron. We test for these and use GFC to rebuild density.

  • Narrower-looking part
  • More volume on top
  • Root causes checked and treated
Often combined withBlood testsPrescribed topicals
Typical sessions4–6, every 4 weeks
Hair treatment in Trivandrum

Thinning crown

The crown is one of the first places to thin and the hardest to see yourself. GFC injections spread across the thin patch improve coverage, so less scalp shows under light.

  • Better crown coverage
  • Thicker strands
  • Easy to track with photos
Often combined withExosomesQR678
Typical sessions4–6, every 4 weeks

Weak, thin hair

Your hair isn't falling in clumps, but your ponytail is thinner or styling doesn't hold like before. This is the best time to act, because every follicle you save now is one you won't need to regrow later.

  • Stronger, thicker strands
  • Saves follicles early
  • Fewer sessions needed
Often combined withNutritionScalp care
Typical sessions3–4, every 4 weeks

Alopecia areata (patchy hair loss)

Round, smooth bald patches are usually alopecia areata, an immune condition. It needs a doctor's diagnosis and medical treatment first. GFC can be added to support regrowth in suitable cases.

  • Doctor diagnosis first
  • Medical treatment as the base
  • GFC as support
ImportantDoctor-led treatment
Typical sessionsPlanned by your doctor

Tried PRP and didn't see enough?

PRP results vary because the number of platelets in your blood varies. GFC uses special tubes to release and concentrate the growth factors before injection, so each session delivers a stronger, more consistent dose.

  • More concentrated than PRP
  • Less swelling and soreness
  • Often fewer sessions

GFC vs PRP: which to choose

Be honest with yourself

What Stage Is Your Hair Loss?

GFC works on follicles that are still alive. The earlier you start, the more hair you keep.

Early thinning

More hair fall, a slightly wider part or a softer hairline. The best time to start GFC.

Best for: hair fall, early thinning
Downtime: none
Sessions: 3–4, every 4 weeks

Moderate thinning

Scalp visible through the hair, thin crown or temples. Still very treatable with GFC.

Best for: pattern thinning, crown
Downtime: none
Sessions: 4–6, plus maintenance

Advanced / bald areas

Smooth, shiny areas where follicles have stopped. GFC can't regrow these, but it can protect the hair around them.

Best for: support, before or after transplant
Downtime: none
Sessions: we'll discuss transplant options honestly

Swipe to see more

GFC vs PRP

How Is GFC Different from PRP?

Both use your own blood. The difference is what goes into your scalp.

PRP (platelet-rich plasma) injects concentrated platelets into the scalp, where they slowly release growth factors.

  • Contains platelets and some white and red cells
  • Growth factor dose depends on your platelet count
  • Can cause more swelling and soreness
  • Usually 4 to 6 sessions, sometimes more
Good for: early hair fall, budget-friendly start
About PRP for hair

GFC releases the growth factors first, then injects only the concentrated, cell-free liquid.

  • Pure growth factors, without platelets or cells
  • More consistent strength from session to session
  • Less swelling, more comfortable recovery
  • Often fewer sessions for similar results
Good for: pattern thinning, crowns, when PRP wasn't enough

What's inside

The Growth Factors in GFC

Tap each one to see what it does for your hair.

PDGF (platelet-derived growth factor)
Helps follicle cells multiply and keeps hair in the growing phase for longer.
VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)
Builds tiny new blood vessels around follicles, so roots get more oxygen and nutrients.
EGF (epidermal growth factor)
Supports the skin cells around the follicle and helps the scalp repair.
IGF-1 (insulin-like growth factor)
Encourages hair to grow longer and thicker and delays the shedding phase.
FGF (fibroblast growth factor)
Helps wake up resting follicles and start new growth.
TGF-β (transforming growth factor beta)
Supports tissue repair and helps balance the hair growth cycle.

Your complete hair plan

GFC Works Best as Part of a Plan

Hair loss rarely has a single cause, so our doctors look at the full picture, not just the scalp.

Before treating, we find out why your hair is falling. Your doctor examines your scalp and may suggest simple blood tests.

  • Haemoglobin, iron and ferritin
  • Vitamin D and B12
  • Thyroid function
  • Hormones and PCOS checks for women
Why it matters: fixing the cause makes GFC work better

Your GFC course delivers concentrated growth factors straight to the roots.

  • 4 to 6 sessions, about 4 weeks apart
  • Progress photos at every visit
  • Maintenance every 3 to 6 months
Time: 45–60 min per session
Downtime: none

What you do between sessions matters. Your doctor may prescribe treatment to use at home.

  • Topical or oral medication if suitable
  • A gentle, scalp-friendly shampoo
  • Supplements only where tests show a need
Tip: never start or stop hair medicines without your doctor

For stubborn pattern hair loss, GFC can be alternated with other regenerative treatments.

  • Exosomes: ready-made growth signals, no blood draw
  • QR678: a growth-factor formula for hair
  • Hair transplant for areas that are fully bald

Your appointment

GFC Hair Treatment Procedure

A proper diagnosis comes first.

  • Your doctor examines your scalp and hair pattern and takes progress photos.
  • Blood tests may be suggested to check iron, vitamins, thyroid or hormones.
  • Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers for a week, if your doctor agrees.
  • Skip smoking and alcohol for a few days before.
  • Eat a proper meal, drink plenty of water and come with a clean, dry scalp.

A session takes 45 to 60 minutes, including preparation.

  • About 20 to 30 ml of blood is drawn from your arm.
  • It's processed in GFC tubes and a centrifuge to release and collect the growth factors.
  • Your scalp is cleaned, and numbing cream applied if you'd like.
  • The concentrate is injected across the thinning areas with a very fine needle.
  • You'll feel small pricks, but most people find it easy.

You can go straight back to your day. The full aftercare plan is below.

  • Mild redness or tenderness for a few hours.
  • Don't wash your hair for 24 hours.
  • Avoid gym, swimming and strong sun on the scalp for 48 hours.
  • Skip hair colour and chemical treatments for a week.
  • Book your next session in about 4 weeks.

Results

GFC Hair Treatment Results Timeline

Hair grows about 1 cm a month, so results build over months. Here's what most people notice.

  1. Weeks 4–8

    Less hair fall

    Fewer hairs in the shower, on your pillow and in your comb.

  2. Month 3

    Baby hairs

    Short new hairs appear along the hairline, parting and crown.

  3. Months 4–6

    Thicker hair

    Stronger strands and fuller-looking hair, with less scalp showing.

  4. After the course

    Maintain

    A session every 3 to 6 months keeps results going.

Illustrative model images. Results vary with the cause and stage of hair loss.

A good fit if you

  • Have more hair fall than usual
  • Notice thinning, a wider part or a thin crown
  • Tried PRP and want stronger results
  • Want a natural treatment with no downtime

Not ideal if you

  • Have fully bald, shiny areas
  • Have a blood or platelet disorder
  • Have an active scalp infection
  • Expect results in a few weeks

Aftercare

GFC Aftercare

A few simple steps help the growth factors work and protect your scalp.

Do

  • Leave your scalp alone
  • Sleep on a clean pillowcase
  • Drink plenty of water
  • Wear a loose cap in strong sun

Avoid

  • Washing your hair
  • Oils, gels, sprays or serums
  • Touching or scratching the scalp
  • Painkillers like ibuprofen, unless your doctor says so

Do

  • Wash with a mild shampoo and lukewarm water
  • Pat hair dry gently
  • Restart prescribed home treatment when advised
  • Eat protein-rich meals

Avoid

  • Gym, swimming and saunas for 48 hours
  • Hair colour, bleach or straightening for a week
  • Smoking and alcohol for a few days
  • Hair oil massages for 3 days

Healthy habits

  • Protein, iron and vitamin-rich food
  • 7 to 8 hours of sleep
  • Manage stress
  • Gentle, wide-tooth combing

Keep up

  • Prescribed home treatment
  • Scalp-friendly shampoo
  • Progress check every few months
  • Maintenance sessions

Myths vs facts

GFC Myths, Busted

"GFC is just another name for PRP."
Both start with your blood, but PRP injects platelets while GFC injects the growth factors already released from them. GFC is more concentrated and cell-free.
"One session is enough."
Hair grows in cycles, so follicles need repeated signals. Most people need 4 to 6 sessions for lasting change.
"GFC can regrow a completely bald head."
GFC revives weak follicles that are still alive. Fully bald, shiny areas usually need a hair transplant.
"Using your own blood is risky."
It's your own blood, processed in sterile, single-use tubes, so there's no risk of allergy or rejection.
"Once treated, hair loss never comes back."
Pattern hair loss is ongoing. Maintenance sessions and home care keep your results going.

Safety first

Side Effects and Who Should Wait

GFC is made from your own blood and is very well tolerated. Here's what's normal and when to check with your doctor first.

Common and temporary

  • Mild redness or tenderness for a few hours
  • Slight swelling at injection points
  • A small bruise where blood was drawn
  • Mild itching as the scalp settles

Talk to your doctor first if you

  • Have a blood, platelet or clotting disorder
  • Take blood thinners
  • Are pregnant or breastfeeding
  • Have a scalp infection or open wound
  • Have cancer, or are on chemotherapy

Questions

GFC Hair Treatment FAQs

What is GFC hair treatment?
GFC stands for Growth Factor Concentrate. A small amount of your blood is processed in special tubes that make platelets release their growth factors. These growth factors are collected and injected into the thinning areas of your scalp to strengthen follicles and boost hair growth.
How is GFC different from PRP?
PRP injects platelets, which release growth factors slowly inside the scalp. GFC releases the growth factors first and injects only the concentrated, cell-free liquid. That means a stronger, more consistent dose and usually less swelling and soreness.
Is GFC better than PRP?
For many people, yes. GFC is more concentrated and often needs fewer sessions. PRP is still a good option for early hair fall and costs less. Your doctor will suggest the best one after examining your scalp.
Is GFC hair treatment painful?
You'll feel small pricks from the fine needle. We can apply numbing cream first. Most people find it easier than PRP because there's less swelling afterwards.
How many GFC sessions will I need?
Most people need 4 to 6 sessions about 4 weeks apart, then a maintenance session every 3 to 6 months. Early hair fall may settle with 3 to 4 sessions.
When will I see results from GFC?
Hair fall usually slows within 4 to 8 weeks. Baby hairs often appear by 3 months, and thicker, fuller hair shows around 4 to 6 months.
Is GFC safe?
Yes. It's made from your own blood, so there's no risk of allergy or rejection. The blood is processed in sterile, single-use tubes. Mild redness or tenderness for a few hours is the most common side effect.
Can GFC regrow hair on a bald patch?
GFC works on follicles that are still alive, even if they're weak. Smooth, shiny bald areas where follicles have gone usually can't regrow with any injection. We'll tell you honestly and discuss options like hair transplant.
Does GFC work for women?
Yes. GFC works well for female pattern thinning, postpartum shedding and stress-related hair fall. We also check iron, thyroid and hormones so the root cause is treated.
Are GFC results permanent?
Results last as long as the cause is managed. Pattern hair loss continues over time, so most people keep their results with maintenance sessions and home care.
Can I take GFC after a hair transplant?
Yes. GFC is often used before and after a transplant to support grafts and protect surrounding hair. Your doctor will time it with your surgeon.
When can I wash my hair after GFC?
Wait at least 24 hours, then use a mild shampoo and lukewarm water.
